Create an interactive pie or donut chart

Source: R/piechart.R
pie_chart.Rd

Draws one slice per category, with its share of the total written on the slice or next to it. Rows with the same label are added up, and the value can be left empty to count rows. Small slices can be combined into an "Other" slice. Set innerRadius to draw a donut chart, whose centre shows the total, or the hovered slice.

Usage

pie_chart(
  data,
  value = NULL,
  label,
  colorCategory = NULL,
  innerRadius = 0,
  outerRadius = "auto",
  padRadius = NULL,
  padAngle = NULL,
  cornerRadius = 0,
  labelFont = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  titleFontSize = 20,
  font = "Verdana, Geneva, Tahoma, sans-serif",
  bgcol = "white",
  opacity = 1,
  labelHeight = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  fill = NULL,
  sort = c("descending", "ascending", "none"),
  maxSlices = NULL,
  otherLabel = "Other",
  labels = NULL,
  labelPosition = c("auto", "inside", "outside"),
  legend = TRUE,
  centerLabel = NULL,
  highlight = NULL,
  startAngle = 0,
  endAngle = 360,
  stroke = NULL,
  strokeWidth = NULL,
  tooltip = TRUE,
  animate = TRUE,
  valueFormat = NULL,
  valuePrefix = "",
  valueSuffix = "",
  subtitle = NULL,
  subtitleFontSize = 13,
  axisCol = "#333333"
)

Arguments

data

The data frame to consider.

value

The name of the numeric variable (the size of the slices). When NULL, the rows of each label are counted. Rows with the same label are added up; negative and missing values are left out.

label

The name of the labelling variable (one slice per value).

colorCategory

Optional. The name of a D3 categorical colour scheme, such as "Tableau10", "Set2" or "Paired" (see <https://github.com/d3/d3-scale-chromatic#categorical>), used when fill is not given. Defaults to the ddplot palette.

innerRadius

The inner radius, for a donut chart: a number below 1 is a fraction of the outer radius (e.g. 0.6), a larger number is a radius in pixels. Defaults to 0 (a pie).

outerRadius

The outer radius in pixels, or "auto" (default) to fill the space available.

padRadius

Optional. From the D3 documentation, the pad radius computes the fixed linear distance separating adjacent arcs, defined as padRadius * padAngle. Defaults to the D3 default.

padAngle

Optional. The padding angle between consecutive slices, in radians (e.g. 0.02).

cornerRadius

The radius of the rounded slice corners, in pixels. Defaults to 0.

labelFont

Optional. The font family of the legend. Defaults to font.

title

Optional. The title of the plot.

titleFontSize

The font size of the plot title. Defaults to 20.

font

The font family to consider for the titles. Defaults to "Verdana, Geneva, Tahoma, sans-serif".

bgcol

The background color of the SVG. Defaults to "white".

opacity

The opacity of the slices (from 0 to 1). Defaults to 1.

labelHeight

Optional. The font size of the legend, in pixels. Defaults to 12.

width

Optional. The width of the SVG output.

height

Optional. The height of the SVG output.

fill

Optional. The colours of the slices: one colour per slice, in the order of the slices (recycled), or a named vector mapping colours to labels.

sort

The order of the slices, clockwise from the top: "descending" (default, largest first), "ascending" or "none" (the order of the data, or of the factor levels).

maxSlices

Optional. The maximum number of slices: the smallest categories are combined into an "Other" slice so that at most maxSlices slices are drawn.

otherLabel

The label of the combined slice. Defaults to "Other".

labels

What to write for each slice: any of "label", "value" and "percent", or "none". Defaults to "percent" with a legend, c("label", "percent") without.

labelPosition

Where the slice labels go: "auto" (default, inside the slices that are large enough, outside with a leader line for the others), "inside" or "outside".

legend

Logical. Show the legend (on the right when there is room, otherwise below). Defaults to TRUE.

centerLabel

For a donut chart, the text shown under the total in the centre: NULL (default, "Total"), a string, or FALSE to leave the centre empty.

highlight

Optional. A character vector of labels whose slices are pulled out.

startAngle, endAngle

The angles where the pie starts and ends, in degrees, clockwise from the top. Defaults to 0 and 360; use -90 and 90 for a half donut.

stroke

The colour of the lines between the slices. Defaults to the background colour.

strokeWidth

The width of the lines between the slices. Defaults to 1.5 (0 when padAngle is given).

tooltip

Logical. Show a tooltip when hovering the slices. Defaults to TRUE.

animate

Logical. Sweep the slices in when the chart is first drawn. Defaults to TRUE.

valueFormat

Optional. A D3 format string for the values, such as ",.0f" or ".2s".

valuePrefix, valueSuffix

Optional. Text added before and after the values, such as "$" or " kg".

subtitle

Optional. A subtitle drawn under the title.

subtitleFontSize

The font size of the subtitle. Defaults to 13.

axisCol

The colour of the texts. Defaults to "#333333".

Value

An interactive SVG pie chart (an r2d3 htmlwidget).

Interactions

  • Hover a slice (or its legend entry) to pull it out and see its value, its share of the total and its rank; the "Other" slice lists the categories it contains.

  • Click a legend entry to hide or show a slice (the shares are then computed without it), double-click it to keep only that slice.

  • Click a slice to pull it out, click it again to put it back.

Shiny

Inside Shiny, with r2d3::d3Output("id") and r2d3::renderD3(), clicking a slice sets input$id_clicked to its label. The hidden slices are kept when the chart is re-rendered.

Examples

library(ggplot2) # needed for the mpg data frame

# Rows are counted when there is no value
pie_chart(mpg, label = "class", title = "Cars by class")



# A donut chart with the total in the centre
energy <- data.frame(
  source = c("Nuclear", "Hydro", "Wind", "Solar", "Gas", "Coal", "Other"),
  twh    = c(320, 58, 49, 23, 34, 3, 8)
)
pie_chart(
  energy, value = "twh", label = "source",
  innerRadius = 0.6, centerLabel = "TWh",
  title = "Electricity generation by source"
)



# A half donut with the small slices combined
pie_chart(
  energy, value = "twh", label = "source",
  innerRadius = 0.55, startAngle = -90, endAngle = 90,
  maxSlices = 4, legend = FALSE
)
